name: Data Handling
what_is_it: Data handling is the process of collecting, organising, summarising and interpreting information. Grade 8 covers measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range), plus reading and drawing graphs.
why_it_matters: Data skills let us make sense of surveys, sports statistics, scientific results, and business figures — and are essential for informed decision-making in nearly every career.
key_vocabulary: Mean — the average: sum of values divided by how many values there are
Median — the middle value when data is arranged in order
Mode — the value(s) that occur most frequently
Range — the difference between the highest and lowest value, showing spread
Frequency — how many times a value or category occurs in the data
core_concept: Mean, median and mode all describe the 'centre' of a data set, but each responds differently to unusual/extreme values (outliers) — choosing the right measure depends on the data and the question being asked.
rules: To find the median, ALWAYS order the data first (ascending).
If there is an even number of data values, the median is the average of the two middle values.
A data set can have no mode, one mode, or several modes (multi-modal).
Mean is affected strongly by outliers; median is not.
formulae: Mean = (sum of all values) ÷ (number of values)
Median (odd n): middle value of ordered data
Median (even n): average of the two middle ordered values
step_by_step_method: STEP 1: Write down all data values.
STEP 2: For median/range, order the data from smallest to largest.
STEP 3: For mean, add all values and divide by the count.
STEP 4: For mode, identify the most frequent value(s).
STEP 5: For range, subtract the minimum from the maximum.
STEP 6: Interpret the results in the context of the question.

worked_example_1.question: Find the mean, median, mode and range of: 4, 8, 6, 8, 3, 9, 8
worked_example_1.solution:
Ordered: 3, 4, 6, 8, 8, 8, 9
Mean = (4+8+6+8+3+9+8)/7 = 46/7 ≈ 6.57
Median = middle value = 8
Mode = 8 (appears 3 times)
Range = 9 − 3 = 6

worked_example_2.question: Find the median of: 12, 15, 9, 20 (even number of values)
worked_example_2.solution:
Ordered: 9, 12, 15, 20
Two middle values: 12 and 15
Median = (12 + 15) ÷ 2 = 13.5

fast_method: Cross off the smallest and largest values from each end of an ordered list simultaneously to quickly narrow in on the median without recounting the whole list each time.
why_fast_method_works: Systematically removing pairs from both ends preserves the middle position, so you reach the median (or middle pair) faster than manually counting positions in a long list.
common_mistakes: Finding the median without ordering the data first.
Forgetting to average the two middle values when there's an even number of data points.
Confusing mode (most frequent VALUE) with frequency (the COUNT itself).
Rounding the mean too early and then using the rounded number in further calculations.
memory_trick: "Mean = share it out equally. Median = the middle after lining up. Mode = the most popular."
visual_explanation: Learnly's Data Lab draws a bar graph or dot plot of the data, visually marking the mean (balance point), median (middle position), and mode (tallest bar).
challenge_question: A class of 5 learners has a mean test score of 70%. A 6th learner joins and the new mean becomes 72%. What mark did the 6th learner get?
mastery_check: Mastered when a student can compute all four measures fluently on unordered raw data, explain in words what each measure represents, and choose the most appropriate measure for a given real-world scenario.
